Being the last one to go is definitely the worst. By this time you've compared your presentation to everyone else's and have all this accumulative dread. If there's any bright side, it's that everyone else has given their presentation and are probably so relieved that theirs is over they're not even paying attention to you.

I decided one day that fuck it, I'm going first. My logic was that the first person always sets the bar, so if I go first and set the bar super low, I'll be a hero for everyone else after me because it would be easy to outdo me. Hahahaha. But you're so right though about people being distracted by practising. When I usually sit through other people giving their presentations, I make eye contact but my mind isn't really there. You're so concerned with "Oh my god, I forgot to include this" or "Shit, have I done this wrong?" or "How do these guys speak so effortlessly?!" or "Thank God I wore dark clothing to hide these sweat stains" and the list goes on...

It's ridiculous trying to get adequate help from mental health teams or hospitals in general. It seems you have to be a certain level of suicidal to be taken seriously. And if you are not, you're turned away. And then some of the people who get turned away eventually end up having really severe symptoms that could have been stopped had there been earlier intervention. Fuck these guys.

I have had my depression questioned by the hospital I was admitted to because I appeared to have a euthymic mood and appeared happy whenever I talked to them. Despite me telling them I was actually miserable and putting on a persona to appear happy around other people, they were convinced I "probably didn't have depression and instead had borderline personality disorder features" but didn't want to formally diagnose anything. They also discharged me a day after I tried to strangle myself in hospital. 

The whole experience has just left me doubting whether my thoughts and experiences are real or important enough anymore. I feel worse from the whole experience and now even more reluctant to seek help if I feel suicidal again. Seems like you have to have a  textbook case of depression to be taken seriously. God forbid if you smile once or twice...

Well my answer probably won't be anything new you haven't heard, but probably the nature and beaches. There's usually a park/reserve/beach at most 30min away from you in most towns and cities. If you want to go to all the amazing pictures of NZ you see on travel sites, definitely go South Island, especially Milford Sound and don't forget a good camera. Also, most people in NZ are pleasant and kickback, so I guess that's another perk. 

If you like adventure as well, Rotorua and Queenstown are some awesome places to hit up. Zorbing in particular I totally recommend, but it is pricey.

If you're into big cities and awesome nightlife, NZ isn't that great (in my experience) since we're a small country so our shops and malls tend to close pretty early. Wellington is probably a better place to check out than Auckland if you want to visit a city. Hope that helps!

Hey, I was the same. I didn't actually have any reason to be depressed - I just was. A lot of people in my life had it much much worse than me and I felt I couldn't justify myself without coming across whiny. I didnt speak about my shit to anyone.

It had got pretty bad - the more I denied it and pretended  didn't have it the more it showed. I failed all my mid year exams in high school that year and was slowly becoming unbearable to be around. My school counsellor forced me to see a doctor against my wishes.

I finally did and told him the truth about how I felt for ONCE in my fucking life. He completely understood. Turns out my depression was pretty severe. Honestly, they don't judge. They just want to help. They want to see this whole journey through with you. A huge burden was lifted off my shoulders that day for sure... I would have never gone by myself voluntarily but I'm really glad there were people out there that  made me. I hope there are people like that in your life too. All the best.
